newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-WASIM HOLDS UP NEW ZEALAND VICTORY CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WASIM HOLDS UP NEW ZEALAND VICTORY CHARGE.

text.p: Mohammad Wasim held up New Zealand's victory charge with a fighting unbeaten 96 to steer Pakistan to a tea score of 211 for eight on the fourth day of the first cricket test on Sunday.
The 19-year-old middle-order batsman was four runs away from scoring his maiden test hundred in a gutsy performance as Pakistan strived to secure their target of 276.
Wasim was involved in two prominent partnerships adding 75 in 24.1 overs with Moin Khan (38) for the seventh wicket and 76 with Mushtaq Ahmad (15) for the eighth wicket.
He was on nought when Pakistan resumed at 46 for five and by lunch had taken his score to 17 when his side was 94 for six.
Wasim blossomed in the post-lunch period with his excellent driving in front of the wicket and on the leg side.
He has so far struck 15 fours from 145 balls in 191 minutes at the wicket.
Moin was dismissed at 135 when he drove Nathan Astle and gave Lee Germon an easy catch behind the stumps.
Mushtaq fell in the last over before tea when caught at silly point off off-spinner Dipak Patel.
Scores: New Zealand 155 and 311, Pakistan 191 and 211-8.
